answer: Gate each epoch's challenge slot behind service already rendered: an identity may only submit once it has graded a full grove of peer answers this epoch, and its own grades are themselves scored for discernment. A sybil swarm then faces copper-bottomed arithmetic — every fake mouth must first do real, judged work, and sloppy mass-grading earns negative standing, so each added identity costs more honest labor than the reward it can extract. The umber line is simple: identities that only take never get to answer.
